source.title: Dual Averaging is Surprisingly Effective for Deep Learning Optimization

record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out performance across optimizers on several tasks, testing whether optimizer choice changes generalization outcomes; it uses different optimizers and task metrics than the claim’s cited comparisons.
record.gate_note: The paper reports optimizer comparisons on held-out task metrics. It does not test memorization of random labels, width, convolutional versus fully connected architecture, batch-size effects, dropout, sharpness measures, or removal of memorized examples. Training-loss values are included only where the paper explicitly compares them with held-out performance.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam with momentum SGD using held-out image-classification accuracy, the method and measure relevant to V4. Its MDA comparisons alone do not test V4's specified Adam-versus-SGD comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors present MDA as a general-purpose optimizer that matches the stronger conventional optimizer across tasks, avoids Adam's sometimes poorer test performance, and works where momentum SGD struggles. Decaying implicit L2 regularization is a proposed explanation, not an established cause.
record.recipe_differences: Introduces Modernized Dual Averaging and compares it with SGD+M and Adam; experiments grid-search step sizes, weight decay, and learning-rate schedules for each method.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset and task; learning-rate schedule and weight-decay tuning; the paper notes Adam's schedule performance differs across tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: On fastMRI reconstruction, Adam and MDA have similar SSIM and both outperform momentum SGD.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer performance depends on the task, including image reconstruction beyond classification.

fits_no_version.finding: MDA and Adam have similar translation BLEU; Adam has lower masked-language-model validation perplexity; MDA has lower Wikitext-103 test perplexity despite higher training loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Nonadaptive MDA can compete with Adam on language tasks, with task-dependent differences in held-out performance.

record.problems: Optimizer comparisons span different tasks and metrics; the RoBERTa experiment uses one seed. Some SGD results in language modeling are cited from prior work. The paper reports standard errors for several comparisons, while the numerical results for other comparisons do not include uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No reported optimizer comparison rows were omitted. The paper's training-loss plots without a corresponding reported held-out comparison were not extracted as separate rows.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and its coexistence with natural-label generalization.
Generalization beyond the width required for interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.

The exact learning-rate-and-schedule-only tuning restriction; controlled comparisons of limited versus broader tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching Adam to SGD; and own-run language-model comparisons reporting held-out performance for both Adam and SGD. Equal or better Adam training performance is not numerically established for the image-classification comparisons.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and compensating recipe changes.
Dropout interventions and their effects on held-out error.
Removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for V4. Cited SGD language results cannot supply its own Adam-versus-SGD evidence. MDA's algorithmic ablations assess the proposed method and do not independently test any listed version.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweeps beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models.

The specific Wilson et al. limited-tuning protocol and broader tuning, decoupled weight decay, switching from Adam to SGD, and language-model cases where Adam beats SGD are not systematically tested. Some SGD comparisons are cited results rather than this study’s own runs.
Large-batch comparisons and adaptations to batch size.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the generalization gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the resulting test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: PreAct ResNet152
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; compared test accuracy against MDA and SGD with momentum.
rows.note: The paper states MDA achieves slightly better accuracy than SGD+M; Adam is also lower than SGD+M. The study grid-searches step-sizes, weight decay, and learning-rate schedules.
rows.check: Adam's accuracy is 0.53 percentage points below momentum SGD, clearly showing the specified direction rather than a partial effect. Tuning includes weight decay as well as learning rates and schedules, so this is broader than V4's limited-tuning condition.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1; Figure 1(a); Appendix C, CIFAR10 setup.

rows.subject: ResNet-50
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; compared test accuracy against MDA and SGD with momentum.
rows.note: The paper says Adam trails far behind and MDA versus SGD+M differs within standard errors. Its setup says no alternate schedule worked well for Adam.
rows.check: Adam's validation accuracy is 3.17 percentage points below momentum SGD; this is an observed effect. Tuning includes weight decay and alternative schedules, extending beyond V4's limited-tuning condition.

source_check.locator_found: Section 4.1; Figure 1(b); Appendix C, ImageNet setup.

rows.subject: VarNet 2.0
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; compared test SSIM against MDA and SGD.
rows.note: The paper says MDA performs slightly better than Adam, with the difference within standard error; SGD performs particularly badly despite learning-rate schedule tuning.
rows.check: MRI reconstruction SSIM is outside V4's image-classification and language benchmarks. The recorded baseline also compares Adam with MDA, rather than SGD. Figure 1(c) reports momentum SGD SSIM of 0.9032, below Adam's 0.9111.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; compared test BLEU against MDA and SGD.
rows.note: The paper says MDA outperforms Adam by 0.20 on the test set; table values show 34.18 versus 34.10. The text says Adam and MDA match in training loss.
rows.check: The own-run comparison is Adam versus MDA; the SGD BLEU of 28.45 is attributed to Yao et al., not this study. The table gives an MDA advantage of 0.08 BLEU, inconsistent with the prose's 0.20. The plotted final training losses are 3.45 for MDA and 3.35 for Adam.

rows.subject: RoBERTa
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; compared validation perplexity against MDA.
rows.note: The paper describes MDA’s 5.3 validation perplexity as broadly comparable to Adam’s 4.95 and says additional tuning may close the small gap. It states the training curves are virtually identical.
rows.check: Adam versus MDA does not establish Adam versus SGD held-out performance. SGD's stated failure has no reported held-out value. Adam's lower perplexity than MDA therefore is not a reversal of V4.

rows.subject: Transformer
rows.operation_detail: Trained with Adam; compared test perplexity against MDA and SGD.
rows.note: The paper says MDA reaches significantly worse training loss than Adam (2.33) yet better test perplexity. The SGD result is identified as reported in Yao et al. (2020), not as a run in this study.
rows.check: The study's own held-out comparison is MDA versus Adam; SGD's 78.5 perplexity is cited from Yao et al. The operation incorrectly describes Adam as the measured subject while the value is MDA's. The prose's 2.33 and 1.51 describe differences: training losses are 6.71 versus 4.38, and test perplexities are 31.54 versus 33.05.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10 PreAct ResNet152 and ImageNet ResNet-50, with step-size, weight-decay, and schedule tuning
relationships.reason: R1–R2 show Adam below momentum SGD: 94.69% versus 95.22% on CIFAR-10 and 73.00% versus 76.17% on ImageNet. The disadvantage persists with tuning broader than the version's limited protocol.
relationships.display_finding: Adam achieved 94.69% accuracy versus momentum SGD's 95.22% on CIFAR-10 and 73.00% validation accuracy versus 76.17% on ImageNet, despite broader tuning.

relation.reason: The study reports its own held-out image-classification results comparing Adam with momentum SGD, directly bearing on V4.

tranche.reason: The direct Adam-versus-momentum-SGD comparisons use the original optimizer-comparison method and held-out classification accuracy measure. Broader tuning changes the tested recipe.

source_check.notes: The broader grid searches establish recipe-specific optimizer ordering; they do not isolate the effect of expanding tuning. ImageNet results use validation images, although Figure 1's caption calls the accuracy test accuracy.
